claim: Ni (2008, via CXO summary): unhedged one-month calls on individual US stocks, Jan 1996-Jun 2005, bought at bid-ask midpoint on expiration Fridays and held to expiry, no ex-dividend stocks, had negative average returns when out of the money; calls >15% OTM averaged -28%. Costs: not included beyond midpoint (midpoint is optimistic). Sample ends before 2015. Maturity 1 month (outside 1-6 month window).
quote: Options out of the money by more than 15% yield an average return of -28%.
title: CXO Advisory summary of Ni (2008) Stock Option Returns: A Puzzle

claim: Ni (2008, via CXO): within one-month unhedged individual-stock calls (1996-2005, midpoint prices, no costs), the higher the strike, the worse the average return; CXO notes using the ask instead may eliminate positive returns for at-the-money and in-the-money calls.
quote: Using the ask price instead may eliminate the positive returns for the at-the-money and in-the-money segments.
title: CXO Advisory summary of Ni (2008)

claim: Goyal-Saretto (via CXO), Jan 1996-Oct 2009, ~200K obs: delta-hedged individual-stock calls lose on average 4.89% of option price from 1.5 months before expiry to expiry (HEDGED: measures volatility cheapness, not an outright buyer's return); returns are mostly gross of costs.
quote: Delta-hedged call options lose on average 4.89% (0.48%) of the option (underlying stock) price from 1.5 months before expiration to expiration.
title: CXO Advisory summary of delta-hedged option returns (Goyal-Saretto type study)

claim: Same study (via CXO): delta-hedged at-the-money call strategy long low-vol/short high-vol stocks, 1.5 months to expiry held one month, earns ~2%/month at partly-gross prices; adding friction of 50-100% of the spread cuts it from ~1% to ~0 (hedged, long-short; not a buyer's return). Sample 1996-2009.
quote: Adding trading friction equal to 50%, 75% or 100% of the closing option bid-ask spread incrementally reduces average profitability from about 1% per month to approximately zero.
title: CXO Advisory summary

claim: Boyer-Vorkink (JF 2014, via CXO), ~1996-2009, unhedged individual-stock options held to expiry at end-of-day midpoints, no transaction fees: high-skewness (lottery-like) options earn far less than low-skewness; spread for 7-day calls is +1.4% vs -35.4% per week, puts -5.6% vs -60.6%. Effect strongest near expiry; puts spread larger than calls. Gives weekly returns at 7-day maturity only in the quoted figure.
quote: the spread is +1.4% minus -35.4%, or +36.8%, for calls expiring in seven days and -5.6% minus -60.6%, or +55.0%, for puts expiring in seven days.
title: CXO Advisory summary of Boyer & Vorkink, Stock Options as Lotteries

claim: Boyer-Vorkink (via CXO): demand for high-skewness options is heavy, with many trades above the bid-ask midpoint, consistent with lottery-like demand; spreads rise sharply with skewness so sellers near bid cannot capture the premium.
quote: a large fraction of trades in high-skewness options occurs above the bid-ask midpoint.
title: CXO Advisory summary of Boyer & Vorkink
